Between 2-5 November, the typhoon made multiple landfalls across the central Philippines (Visayas) with wind speeds equivalent to a Category 2 hurricane. An estimated 4.2 million people have been affected compounding the impacts of multiple recent typhoons, floods, and two earthquakes in the same region. Flash floods contributed to the high death toll, with over 230 dead and over 100 people still missing. Over 350,000 people are displaced. For some, such as in Cebu and Negros Occidental, this is expected to be protracted given widespread flooding destroyed 25,000 houses and damaged 200,000 houses and infrastructure. Through contribution to WFP,  2,520 households (approximately 12,600 people) will be provided with two monthly cycles of multi-purpose cash assistance. WFP has a strong partnership with the Department for Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and has the systems in place to rapidly deliver cash via top-ups to 4Ps beneficiaries, which it successfully undertook last year with FCDO funding.

To transform how developing countries access climate finance, in turn supporting implementation of more ambitious and integrated climate action.  The programme will offer governments access to faster and more efficient funding to deliver their national climate & development plans. For example, donor climate finance will be coordinated and mobilised to deliver a national strategy (like the UK’s Ten Point Plan for a Green Industrial Revolution); the strengthening of a specific sector (e.g. improving the resilience of the water sector); or delivering a package of policy actions (e.g. for a clean energy transition). The project will consolidate the achievements in the field of civic/democratic education from the previous interventions. It will support voters to be able to assess and understand the complexities of the electoral environment. The higher level of understanding of the electoral environment will enable people to: 
a.)Take a fully informed decision in any electoral process, and
b.)Develop trust in the democratic system – a key point for democratic stabilisation.

titles: ARM: Promoting of accountability and public oversight of Public Procurement (UIC)
descriptions: Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Armenia Deputy Minister of Finance asked Good Governance Fund to support the procurement reforms. The project implemented by Union of Informed Citizens on-governmental organization will strengthen civil society organizations' role in procurement monitoring and will help the Government of Armenia to improve the public procurement system. Government of Armenia express interest to establish mechanisms for “independent” sources of funding to qualified civil society organizations to carry out procurement monitoring. It will increase public oversight and improve accountability and will also contribute to increased oversight by the civil society and the media.
The project will strengthen CSOs role in procurement monitoring and will help the GoA to improve the Armenian public procurement system.

titles: AZE: Young Agripreneurs (FSIC)
descriptions: The project implemented by Finance and Social Innovation Consulting will support poverty and inequality reduction by growing incomes for up to 500 farmers and by facilitating a new generation of 240 young agripreneurs through the promotion of innovative and sustainable farming techniques, technologies and digitalization and better engagement between the state and citizens through strengthened public and private dialogues. Project’s target groups will be Young women and men living in rural areas of southern region of Azerbaijan who are or want to engage in new generation of agripreneurship; rural households; agriculture value chain players.

The project will support poverty and inequality reduction by growing incomes for up to 500 farmers and by facilitating a new generation of 240 young agripreneurs through the promotion of innovative and sustainable farming techniques, technologies and digitalization and better engagement between the state and citizens through strengthened public and private dialogues.

titles: GEO: Building the Capacity of Civil Society to Mitigate Election Crises (IFES)
descriptions: The 2024 Georgia parliamentary elections present an important opportunity for Georgian democratic stakeholders to strengthen electoral integrity, prevent democratic backsliding, and reduce corrosive dialogue. The International Foundation for Electoral Systems will partner with local civil society organisations to bolster their ability to navigate and adapt to Georgia’s challenging and fluid political environment; engage with citizens and stakeholders; and deliver meaningful oversight of political actors and electoral processes. The International Foundation for Electoral Systems will provide training on elections technology; tailored information and education for voters; and enhanced civil society organisations capacity to identify and respond to electoral crises approaches ahead of the 2024 parliamentary elections.

The project will strengthen the overall resilience of CSOs ahead of and during the 2024 parliamentary election by improving their technical knowledge and outreach around new electoral changes; bolstering their capacity to identify, mitigate, and respond to electoral and political crises; and improving their operational resilience.

titles: GEO: Contributing to more transparent and inclusive electoral process through 2024 Parliamentary elections observation (GYLA)
descriptions: The project implemented by Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association is designed to bolster the transparency, fairness, and overall integrity of the electoral process in the country through the observation of elections by independent and objective watchdog organisation. With a total of 600 observers set to be deployed across the nation, this specific project aims to support 150 of these observers through comprehensive training programs and deploy them on the election day. Moreover, the project will cover the pre-election, e-day and post-election period to assess overall organisation of electoral process in Georgia. Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association’s observation mission will consist of: 80 precinct, precinct perimeter, and mobile group observers, 30 district observers, 40 headquarters members. Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association will also litigate cases on problematic areas in elections apparent through the short-term and long-term missions. Based on the findings of the election observation mission and in parallel with it, Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association will continue advocating its recommendations to the decision-making bodies (Central Election Commission and the Parliament) to improve the electoral system in Georgia.

titles: GEO: Enhancing Citizen Observation of the 2024 Parliamentary Elections in Georgia (ISFED)
descriptions: The project implemented by the International Society for Fair Elections and Democracy will focus on monitoring the immediate vicinity of polling stations. With the deployment of 200 carefully selected and trained short-term observers, International Society for Fair Elections and Democracy will have the ability to document and report irregularities during the electoral process, ensuring that citizens' rights are safeguarded. This project aims to increase reputation costs for political actors engaged in malicious practices, increase public awareness of election-related violations, and thus promote more fair and trustworthy elections. This initiative will lead to a more transparent and just electoral and political environment that accurately reflects citizens' votes.

titles: MOL: Advanced Capacities for Trade project (AdTrade)
descriptions: The Advanced Capacities for Trade project has been uniquely designed to contribute to a host of complex and inter-linked goals, aiming at supporting an environment of trust and cooperation across the post-conflict divide through capitalizing on the opportunities offered by the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area and SPTCA, while consolidating trade ties across the river and with the European Union, and supporting economic growth that benefits the most vulnerable. The project represents a framework for engaging in development interventions on both sides of the Nistru River, primarily focusing at improving the livelihoods of the people from both sides of the Nistru River through their mutual cooperation.

titles: GEO Legal advice to support work with CSOs in Georgia (BGI Legal)
descriptions: Within the scope of the existing Contract with the local legal consulting company, we will seek legal advice on the ways of working with Civil Society Organisations in Georgia considering the challenging political developments (adoption of the law on Transparency of Foreign Influence in the country). The UK has a clear commitment as set out in the Integrated Review to “work with allies, like minded partners and civil society worldwide to protect democratic values” and to “defend universal human rights.” Thus, the advice from the legal consultants will provide options of enhancing our support to the Civil Society on the ground.

titles: MOL: Media Enabling Democracy, Inclusion, and Accountability in Moldova(MEDIA-M)
descriptions: The Media Enabling Democracy, Inclusion and Accountability in Moldova project implemented by United States Agency for International Development, aims to promote the development of an independent, professional media that gives citizens access to a variety of perspectives and to create a media sector that is more resilient to political and financial pressures. By focusing on the supply of and demand for objective information, this Activity will strengthen the ability of independent media to fulfil its role as a watchdog over the government and serve as a space for citizens to engage in public policy dialogue. Moreover, the Activity’s focus on the legal enabling environment will reinforce existing protections for freedom of speech, facilitate better implementation of laws, and advocate for media sector regulation in accordance with international norms.

titles: MOL: Support for civic observation of the 2024 Presidential Elections and Constitutional Referendum in Moldova (Promo-LEX)
descriptions: Promo-LEX Association aims to conduct an Election Observation Mission in the context of Moldova’s Presidential elections and Constitutional Referendum scheduled for October 20, 2024. The Mission will oversee the electoral process to ensure transparency, credibility, and democratic integrity, addressing key challenges such as social and political tensions, external influence from Russia, and political corruption. Given the high stakes, particularly regarding Moldova's European integration, this observation mission will cover all election stages, from pre-election developments to post-election outcomes. Activities include recruiting and training a robust network of observers, analysing legal and socio-political contexts, and conducting both qualitative and quantitative monitoring.

titles: MOL: Providing Observers for Presidential Elections in Moldova (WFD)
descriptions:
On 20th of October 2024, Moldova will hold its next presidential elections and a constitutional referendum on accession to the European Union. It is expected that Moldova will request OSCE to send an election observation mission (EOM) funded by member states, including the UK.
Given the challenges outlined in the 2023 local elections, the context of foreign interference, illegal financing, disinformation, cyber-attacks, and hybrid threats, there is a need for proactive support and assistance to electoral integrity in Moldova. Election observation missions are crucial to assess the extent to which elections respect fundamental freedoms based on equality, universality, political pluralism, transparency and accountability. 
The proposed intervention will complement ongoing HMG’s electoral support in Moldova through the GGF project on enhancing democracy in Moldova through inclusive and transparent elections, implemented by UNDP. It will contribute to the GGF country level priority for stronger and more independent electoral stakeholders to ensure the public can hold the government accountable, in line with the GGF Theory of Change, Elections Theory of Change and the Country Business Plan.

titles: GEO: OSCE ODIHR for the Georgian Election Observation Mission (WFD)
descriptions: The British Embassy Tbilisi seeks to meet the UK’s commitment to supporting OSCE/ODIHR election observation by providing Long-term Observers and Short-Term Observers to the OSCE/ODIHR election observation mission for Parliamentary Elections in Georgia, October 2024. The Supplier should provide high quality observers to the ODIHR EOM. They should be able to navigate the ODIHR nomination and registration system in order to secure places for UK observers in the mission, and liaise effectively with ODIHR to ensure the timely arrival and induction of observers.

titles: ARM: Promoting of accountability and public oversight of Public Procurement
descriptions:
The project will strengthen CSOs role in procurement monitoring and help the GoA improve the Armenian public procurement system.  

It should be noted that due to the joint efforts of the Union of Informed Citizens NGO and the RA Ministry of Finance, the possibilities to oversee the handover and acceptance of procurement were significantly simplified for civil society and media. During the session of the Government on May 23 2024, the issue of making amendments and addenda to N526-N Decision of the RA Government of May 4 2017 was discussed and adopted. According to the amendments, procurement oversight opportunities are significantly simplified for civil society and media representatives, and now they have the opportunity to oversee the procurement acceptance process through simplified mechanisms and to supervise the construction process of schools, kindergartens and hospitals etc. 

The policy changes that the organization was able to achieve due to the previous project will yield the potential results. The project will increase public oversight improve accountability and develop the capacity of CSOs and media by providing relevant knowledge and skills that will create cooperation between the GoA and CSOs and media in the future.

titles: REG: Programme Manager for EBRD-UK Investment Climate and Governance Fund
descriptions: Programme Manager's position to lead on and manage implementation of the EBRD-UK Investment Climate and Governance Fund programme within the extended period of 9 months.

titles: ARM: Promoting Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Through Community Budgeting (OxYGen)
descriptions: The project aims to promote gender equality and social inclusion in Armenia by ensuring that community budgets fairly address the needs of all groups, especially women, girls, and the Yezidi community. This will be done by both building the capacities of LSGs in the project target regions, increasing the participation of marginalized groups in decision-making, and supporting civil society to advocate for fairer and more inclusive budget policies.

titles: ARM: Demographic Resilience: Expanding Women's Capacities and Choices through Data-driven Policies (UNFPA)
descriptions:
This project aims to enhance Armenia’s demographic resilience and economic growth by empowering women through lifelong education, gender-responsive policy-making, and evidence-based strategies to address gender disparities in the labor market and beyond.
Through collaboration with key stakeholders including the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports, Yerevan State University, United Social Services and the Armenian National Statistical Committee, as well as civil society organizations, this project will utilize innovative methodologies such as National Time Transfer Accounts (NTTA) to provide critical insights into gendered labor dynamics. A key component of this initiative is the support to development of a Demographic Center within Yerevan State University, which will drive research, policy analysis, and data collection. Additionally, the project will strengthen Armenia’s national data management capacity to support evidence-based policy development that strengthens gender-responsive demographic resilience. In its pilot phase, the project will implement a component focused on lifelong learning, supporting women’s (re)entry into the labour market, and enhancing their knowledge and skills. In all, the project thus will have a sustainable impact on policy making, capacity building of state systems and infrastructure and paving a way for greater empowerment for women

titles: MOL: Moldova Elections Support Project (MESP) (IFES)
descriptions:
This project will strengthen Moldova’s electoral system by enhancing political finance enforcement, securing emerging technologies, and improving postal voting integrity. These efforts will equip the CEC with the tools and expertise to counter malign influence, increase transparency, and ensure elections are fair and free from undue influence. Activities under Output 1 will enable the CEC to audit party finances more effectively, audit political advertising, and enforce financial transparency, reducing the impact of illicit funding in elections. Output 2 will ensure election stakeholders can mitigate risks posed by emerging technologies, including AI and cyber threats, through targeted training and technical assistance. Output 3 will improve the credibility of postal voting by training officials, strengthening cybersecurity, and launching public awareness campaigns. Finally, Output 4 will ensure continuous
support to election administration officials through electoral dialogues, stakeholder coordination, and post-election assessments, reinforcing long-term resilience.
During this critical parliamentary election period, this project will contribute to a more transparent and credible electoral process, fostering greater public trust and strengthening Moldova’s democratic foundations. By reducing vulnerabilities to foreign interference and corruption, Moldova will be better positioned for EU integration. electoral process, fostering greater public trust and strengthening Moldova’s democratic foundations. By reducing vulnerabilities to foreign interference and corruption, Moldova will be better positioned for EU integration.

titles: MOL: Democracy in Action: strengthening electoral integrity, political accountability, and civic participation (Promo-LEX)
descriptions:
This project is designed to strengthen Moldova’s democratic institutions, safeguard electoral integrity, and foster greater civic participation in the lead-up to and beyond the 2025 parliamentary elections. By addressing key vulnerabilities within the electoral process, political accountability, and public engagement, the project aims to reinforce Moldova’s democratic foundations and ensure a more transparent and participatory political environment.  
A core focus of the initiative is on electoral integrity and independent observation, ensuring that elections are conducted fairly and transparently. Through rigorous monitoring, the project will help detect and prevent fraud, vote-buying, and foreign interference, which have increasingly threatened Moldova’s democratic processes. Alongside these efforts, the project will advocate for greater transparency in political financing and stronger enforcement of anti-corruption regulations. By supporting legislative improvements and reinforcing parliamentary oversight mechanisms, it will contribute to enhancing the accountability of political institutions.  
In parallel, the project will work to increase civic engagement by implementing widespread voter education and Get Out The Vote (GOTV) initiatives. Public awareness campaigns will provide citizens with accurate information about the electoral process while mobilizing key demographic groups.  
Through these targeted interventions, the project will help build a more informed electorate, restore public trust in democratic institutions, and contribute to Moldova’s long-term commitment to European integration. By promoting electoral transparency and reinforcing institutional resilience, this initiative will play a crucial role in shaping a stable and democratic future for the country.

titles: MOL: Critical Relief for Independent Media in Moldova (CRIMM) (Internews Europe)
descriptions:
CRIMM will manage a grant pool of up to £136,500 to support national and regional KPs previously supported through USAID and UK government funding. These KPs, who have been operating for between five to 27 years, have established brands and audiences, and the potential to expand their reach, influence, and sustainability. The project will help to stabilise their operations, sustain and improve their content production capabilities at a time when independent media coverage is critically needed. It will also lay individual paths to business and operational models less dependent on donor funding.
Grant support will be customised for each partner based on individual priority areas identified in their 2024 Media Specific Organisational Capacity Assessment (M-OCA). Internews and KPs will jointly identify priority needs and develop individual capacity development plans. Grants assistance will cover essential operational needs (such as salaries, office rent, relocation, legal fees, digital security and journalistic tools) to ensure the continuous production of timely, high-quality information. To ensure proper implementation of the milestones, Internews will require each grantee to allocate funds for consultant and mentor support.

titles: GEO: UN Georgia Thematic Pooled Fund on Civic Space Trust Fund Contirbution
descriptions: Strengthening civic engagement and participation in public life on the national level and facilitating citizens’ access to information through pluralistic media are often seen as major instruments to address problems of democratic backsliding and the need to revitalize societal support for democratic processes and institutions. UN in Georgia will mobilize resources under three distinct funding windows: 1) Enhanced citizens’ awareness and participation in public life; 2) Enhanced skills, capacities and resilience of civic actors to engage with their communities and to participate in decision making process; 3) Enhanced media environment for public deliberation and evidence informed policy discussions to ensure a systematic and integrated approach to the challenges that civil society faces.

titles: ARM: Increasing Women’s Political Participation in Armenia (NDI)
descriptions: Despite the promises of the 2018 revolution for a new style of politics, political parties remain largely consolidated among a small group of male leaders, limiting the emergence of new voices and hindering the advancement and meaningful political participation of women. With gender quotas in place and a growing commitment from party leadership to fostering a bench of strong women candidates, the upcoming 2026 national and local elections present a key opportunity for improving women’s political participation as candidates. The National Democratic Institute (NDI)’s program would support the development, integration, and elevation of women candidates within political parties ahead of the 2026 parliamentary elections.

titles: MOL: Providing Observers for Parliamentary Elections in Moldova (WFD)
descriptions: The British Embassy Chisinau seeks to meet the UK’s commitment to supporting OSCE/ODIHR election observation by providing Long-term Observers (LTOs) to the OSCE/ODIHR election observation mission (EOM) for the Parliamentary Election in Moldova on 28 September 2025. The main beneficiaries of this work will be OSCE/ODIHR, whose mission will benefit from the expertise of the UK observers, and the Moldovan electorate, whose confidence in the electoral process will be increased by the presence of a strong contingent of international observers.

titles: ARM: Resilient Voices: Strengthening Public Interest Media for Armenia’s 2026 Elections (MIC)
descriptions:
The project will strengthen the sustainability of public interest media, enabling them to produce independent, high-quality content and address funding challenges. By improving financial viability and enhancing editorial standards, the project will empower public with reliable, evidence-based information, particularly important ahead of the 2026 parliamentary elections.

Six media outlets, selected through an open call, will produce high-quality, evidence-based content on democracy, human rights, election issues. This will provide the public with in-depth analysis, bridge gaps, and support informed decision-making in the election context. Outlets will receive tailored mentorship and training from international experts on audience engagement, monetization, and operational efficiency, leading to innovative business models for long-term resilience.

titles: ARM: Towards Greater Political Integrity in Armenia (TIAC)
descriptions:
This project addresses key challenges of political integrity that undermine the quality of elections in Armenia, including opaque political financing, misuse of administrative resources, third party campaigns, and politically-biased observation.  These issues threaten public trust, distort democratic competition, and remain insufficiently addressed despite recommendations from independent domestic and international observation missions.

The project will promote integrity in politics ahead of 2026 parliamentary elections through enhanced transparency of political party finances and accountable use of administrative resources.

titles: MOL: Innovate Moldova: Strengthen Moldova’s innovation ecosystem and business resilience for sustainable growth (FAM)
descriptions: Moldova is contending with war-related shocks, energy price volatility, and inflation while fast-tracking alignment with the European Union acquis. These pressures expose structural weaknesses: an innovation ecosystem that is still maturing, firms with limited capacity to meet EU standards and trade digitally, growing cyber risks, and uneven uptake of trusted digital public services. The suspension of USAID support to the former Future Technologies Activity created financing gaps just as key reforms and assets—media and ICT skills pipelines, e-commerce regulation and firm adoption, cybersecurity training, and business-facing modules of the EVO application—needed consolidation and scale. Innovate Moldova maintains momentum, but several high impact workstreams remain underfunded, risking loss of earlier UK/FTA gains and slowing EU market integration. The objective of this project is to close these gaps rapidly through a focused UK add-on delivered inside Innovate Moldova’s architecture: strengthen institutions and service delivery (centres, BSOs, associations, EVO), raise firm competitiveness and export readiness (e-commerce, certifications, promotion), and build cyber resilience and skills (basic and advanced courses). This directly addresses the identified problems and advances Good Governance Fund outcomes on accountable reform, inclusive economic resilience, and resilience to hostile threats, with strong engagement of civil society and the private sector.

titles: REG: EN Regional Development Conference
descriptions: EN Regional Development Conference aims to gather programme teams across the region to identify how the future development programme and team will look like and what would be ways of working. The conference will also cover development expertise partnership approach.

titles: MOL: Youth Catalysts: Strengthening Moldova's Democratic Core (UNFPA)
descriptions:
Moldova’s EU integration depends not only on institutional reforms but also on addressing the social drivers that weaken democratic resilience. This project will foster a more resilient and inclusive democracy at the community level, directly addressing youth disengagement and outmigration while embedding good-governance principles that reinforce trust in democratic institutions and advance Moldova’s EU aspirations.
Among the most pressing concerns is youth outmigration: one in three young Moldovans intend to leave, citing disconnection, lack of voice, and limited opportunities for civic and economic participation. Political engagement remains fragile with youth turnout at only 26% in the 2023 local elections.  Exclusion is sharpest among NEET youth, rural girls, and young people with disabilities. Key drivers include limited local economic opportunities; weak civic/political education; low intergenerational dialogue and adult gatekeeping; inaccessible services and transport (especially for youth with disabilities); and perceptions that public institutions are unresponsive.
The project scales up proven, inclusive models of youth empowerment and civic participation to address these drivers directly.

titles: AZE: Feasibility study for the Integrated water supply infrastructure for the greater Baku area (EBRD)
descriptions:
The Project incorporates seven integrated infrastructure works covering key supply lines, drinking water treatment facilities, and ancillary hydraulic structures that supply potable water to Baku city and the Absheron peninsula. The proposed Feasibility Study is a technical assistance assignment that will support the Bank in undertaking detailed assessments required to prepare, structure, and appraise the Project in line with the relevant requirements of the EBRD.

The Project is expected to finance the rehabilitation of three main water supply pipelines, overhaul and reconstruction of drinking water treatment facilities at source locations and development of reservoirs and supporting hydraulic structures that are essential for delivery of water to the most densely population and economically significant part of Azerbaijan. The Project is also expected to include digital measures including smart water metering and sensors. The final scope and structure of the Project will be confirmed upon full completion and approval of the Feasibility Study.

titles: REG: Contribution to the Public-Private Infrastructure Advisory Facility Multi-Donor Trust Fund (Azerbaijan and Armenia)
descriptions:
The Public-Private Infrastructure Advisory Facility (PPIAF) is a World Bank-managed trust fund that provides technical assistance to governments to mobilize private financing and develop public-private partnerships (PPPs) for infrastructure projects. PPIAF addresses the policy, regulatory, and institutional environment needed to attract private investment and ensure sustainable project delivery.
Support through PPIAF would enable countries to strengthen its legal, regulatory, and institutional frameworks for PPPs, improve procurement and risk management systems, and build government capacity to structure bankable projects. This is critical for leveraging private capital for large-scale connectivity initiatives under the Crossroads of Peace.
PPIAF is already active in Azerbaijan meaning it could deploy a regional lens to Armenia’s efforts.

titles: Supporting Judicial Administration Reform in Ukraine (IDLO)
descriptions: The Good Governance Fund seeks to tackle corruption, improve the business environment, make governments more responsive to citizens, enhance media and civil society freedoms, and promote overall reform.

The project will work on the eradication of an entrenched system of state-sponsored corruption and graft which was one of the core demands of the 2014 Revolution of Dignity, with the judiciary considered an enabling layer of this broader system. Local and national-level networks of oligarchic influence and control over the judiciary established since the fall of the Soviet Union have significantly undercut transparency and independence of judicial decisions, resulting in low levels of trust among Ukrainian citizens in their justice system, a general sense of impunity, and state capture. The legislative breakthrough presented by the adoption of draft laws 3711-D and 5068 provides a rare opportunity for an effective relaunch of the judicial reform with the most substantive concerns effectively addressed.All activities and outputs delivered through this technical assistance project contribute to overall judicial reform and are ultimately intended to facilitate to the realization of the goal of strengthened transparency and accountability of Ukraine’s judicial administration. IDLO anticipates that notable inroads towards the realization of the above goal will be made by resuming all judicial appointments in Ukraine in line with transparency and merit-based selection criteria, and by considering and deciding disciplinary complaints against sitting judges in a transparent way (Intermediate Outcomes 1 and 2).

titles: Promoting Integrity in the Public Sector (Pro-Integrity)
descriptions: Promoting Integrity in the Public Sector (Pro-Integrity) program addresses the root causes of corruption and tackles corruption risks at the national institutional level, at the local government level, and in issues related to Ukraine's recovery and reconstruction.The project will focus on: strengthen national level anti-corruption institutional capacity to advance corruption prevention, detection, and deterrence; strengthen anti-corruption compliance and control in local governance; and advance transparency and accountability in resilience, recovery, and reconstruction efforts.

titles: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) secondments
descriptions: Following the OECD council’s recognition of Ukraine as a prospective member, and its request to engage with Ukraine in an initial accession dialogue, OECD members  have requested that the secretariat prepare a 4-year Country Programme for Ukraine. A country programme consists of reviews and other projects; OECD instruments to which Ukraine could adhere; and targets for enhancing Ukraine's participation status in OECD bodies. These are all benchmarks for reform. The Foreign Secretary committed  to the UK funding 2 secondments to support this programme up to 2 years.

titles: Ukraine: inclusive economic recovery and reform event at Wilton Park
descriptions: Follow up from 2024 conference to bring GoU, donors and civil society together to discuss how to move Ukraine towards a modernised, reformed, and inclusive economy resilient to Russian threats and domestic corruption.

titles: Fair Oversight and Reform for Transparent, Inclusive and Free Elections in Ukraine (FORTIFY)
descriptions: The Project aims to improve  Ukraine’s electoral integrity and democratic resilience by advocating for a robust legal framework, enhancing political and security analysis, combating election-related disinformation, and organizing nationwide election observation missions for the post-war elections.

titles: Policy Design Support for the Prime Minister of Ukraine
descriptions: The project aims to support the launch of the Prime Minister’s Key Priorities Delivery Unit. Kyiv School of Economics  Institute team will help build the Unit, provide policy design expertise, and test practical approaches with ministries. This work will lay the foundation for a system that uses evidence-based methods, including behavioural insights, to raise execution of governmental priorities, public awareness of reforms and strengthen trust.

titles: Regional Missing Persons - Western Balkans
descriptions: The aim of this project is to ensure an effective, sustainable, multilateral, rule-of-law-based cooperation mechanism – Missing Persons Group – to account for persons missing from armed conflicts in the former Yugoslavia, where men comprise the larger proportion of the missing, led by the domestic institutions for missing persons of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Montenegro and Serbia, in which – primarily women - among families of the missing are actively engaged.

titles: Support for the development of North Macedonia 2022-2042 National Development Strategy – Phase III
descriptions: Technical assistance to the national institutions in preparation of the first version of the National Development Strategy 2022-2042 for North Macedonia.

titles: Gender gap action – enabling equal opportunities for girls and young women in North Macedonia
descriptions: Work with the national youth network to support girls and young women in North Macedonia to become more active in society, to overcome the gender roles of the patriarchal society and to have equal access to opportunities in the private sector, public and political life, and in decision-making processes at local and national level.

titles: Citizens Engagement for Increased Trust in Government in North Macedonia
descriptions: This project aims to contribute to increased public trust through improved governance and public engagement.

titles: Reinventing Governance in North Macedonia
descriptions: Strengthening democratic governance of central Government institutions through introduction of Key Performance Indicators, implementation of Functional Analysis, strategic planning and plans for Performance management that identify accountability and responsibility lines.

titles: Civil Society Organisations Action for Energy Transition - Serbia
descriptions: The project strives to contribute towards a change in democratic culture in the field of energy, climate and environment through increased public demand for transparency and participation in ongoing reforms. CSOs, trade unions and citizens equipped with knowledge and skills to monitor and influence development of energy and climate policies, together with inputs and support from expert community, will jointly utilise opportunities for participation in the decision-making processes to advocate for ambitious climate targets, decarbonisation and decentralisation of Serbia’s energy system.

titles: Increasing transparency and accountability in Public Financing (CSOs and Media) - Serbia
descriptions: Overall outcome of the project is to create conditions for transparent and accountable distribution of public funds through open calls.  This will be achieved through: a) Increased availability of data on public spending and undue influence through open calls, b) Enhanced ability of stakeholders to provide data-driven oversight and influence over the process, c) Improved regulatory framework and practice of financing independent media and CSOs through open calls and d) Public pressure generated for implementing open calls in line with the public interest.

titles: Strengthening citizen engagement and participation in public policy processes in Serbia
descriptions: The project will contribute to more participatory and active communities in Serbia by supporting 40 CSOs/initiatives to improve their capacity to engage citizens, to research public policies and to advocate for positive change in at least 15 local communities in Serbia.

titles: Fight Against Gender Based Violence and Femicides in the Western Balkans
descriptions: This projects supports gender equality and tackling Gender Based Violence across the Western Balkans through analysis of handling of cases of femicides; review of caselaw in cases of Gender Based Violence; targeted training for judiciary and other institutions within the justice system on applying international best practice; and annual review of practice by the European Court of Human Rights.

titles: Dealing with Conflict Legacy in Kosovo
descriptions: The project works to foster a conducive environment, based on trust and recognition of conflict legacies, contributing to community resilience. At the outcome-level the project aims to build trust and foster social cohesion, through improved interactions between families of the missing persons and wider community. The outcome will be achieved by addressing the need for a strengthened ability of civil society to engage with a unified voice with policy makers, and strengthened community resilience which builds inclusive and constructive narratives of the past.

titles: Supporting institutions and communities building an inclusive society in Kosovo
descriptions: The objective of the project is to support integration and social cohesion in Kosovo through enhancing capacities of central institutions to: provide learning of official languages at University and high-school level, support the process for verification of University and high-school diplomas, develop a mechanism to support monitoring of the implementation of communities-focussed legislation and support the government in addressing issues.

titles: Ensuring CRSV Survivors rights on Justice and Redress in BiH are advanced in accordance with International Standards
descriptions: The project will build up on the previously achieved results with TRIAL International and will develop sustainable and new assistance schemes for Conflict Related Sexual Violence (CRSV) survivors in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The project will also engage in know how sharing with NGOs and international organizations in Ukraine, which will need assistance in providing comprehensive support to CRSV survivors.

titles: Increased government accountability through a more responsive parliament - Albania
descriptions: This project will support strengthening of Albanian Parliamentary oversight functions, particularly to create legal frameworks that guide how matters should be addressed in legislation; to scrutinise programmes, policies and expenditure enacted by government; and to facilitate public participation and discussion over any and all matters of societal concern.

titles: Increase parliament’s responsiveness to citizens’ concerns - Albania
descriptions: This project will support strengthening of Albanian Parliamentary oversight functions in relation to citizens' engagement; to facilitate public participation and discussion over any and all matters of societal concern.

titles: Srebrenica Memorial: Truth, Dialogue, Future - BiH
descriptions: This project aims to build the institutional capacities of the Srebrenica Memorial Centre in order to establish a globally relevant centre for genocide research and prevention, as well as a regional hub for reconciliation and inter-ethnic dialogue.

titles: University and Gender Mainstreaming – UNIGEM - BiH
descriptions: The project aims to build ethos of gender equality in higher education in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) through policy development and sensitisation of teachers and students for sexual harassment and gender-based violence (GBVSH) in cooperation with universities, pedagogical institutes and ministries of education in BiH and three universities from Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro.

The project aims to build ethos of gender equality in higher education in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) through policy development and sensitization of teachers and students for sexual harassment and gender-based violence (GBVSH) in cooperation with universities, pedagogical institutes and ministries of education in BiH and three universities from Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro.

titles: Improving public space and public discourse in Mostar - BiH
descriptions: This project aims to contribute towards a sustainable and inclusive peace in Mostar as a microcosm of Bosnia and Herzegovina, providing hope and inspiration to the wider Western Balkans region.

titles: Safeguarding women and girls in Serbia
descriptions:
To support national and local-level authorities and stakeholders to become more responsive to violence against women and girls in public spaces. Through a first-of-its kind survey, assess the safety of women (e.g. on public transportation, walking alone at night) and work with community groups, CSOs and local municipalities to find local and national solutions. 
The project also seeks to improve accessibility to shelters for survivors of domestic violence and Gender Based Violence, in line with international standards.

titles: Independent, accountable, meritocratic and professional recruitment in Kosovo
descriptions: Offer technical assistance to Kosovo recruitment panels in central and local level to design and implement fair and meritocratic recruitment processes for senior officials, inclusive to all genders and minority groups. Make the results of such meritocratic recruitments public so that decisions makers are able and willing to appoint highest performing candidates. Track and support successful appointees to bring about better governance in the institutions they lead with.

titles: Strengthening of public procurement system in Kosovo
descriptions: The aim of this project is to strengthen public procurement system in Kosovo, to reduce incidents of malfeasance and corruption, while at the same time increasing opportunities for women’s access to contracts. In doing so, the project seeks to improve practices implemented by contracting authorities to ensure level playing field and work with Procurement Review Body (decision-making panel, and administration) to ensure professional and fair adjudication of procurement disputes

titles: Prevention Against Gender Based Violence in North Macedonia
descriptions: Support the Government in North Macedonia to embed and begin implementing state-wide integrated policies on Gender Based Violence

titles: Supporting Media Development and Civil Society in the Western Balkans
descriptions: Providing capacity building support to independent media and civil society actors in the Western Balkans

titles: Western Balkans: Investing in Democratic Resilience
descriptions: The framework will focus on three key objectives: (1) Democratic actors and institutions are more resilient; (2) Western Balkans democratic institutions become more inclusive and representative of marginalised groups, including women and youth; (3) Western Balkans democratic institutions work in more transparent and deliberative way in the interest of citizens.

titles: Addressing effects of sexual violence and ending stigma that survivors face in Kosovo
descriptions: Empowerment of women and girls through tackling Conflict Related Sexual Violence (CRSV), Gender Based Violence (GBV) and promoting women’s meaningful participation in decision-making processes.

titles: Amplifying Local Voices for Equitable Development (ALVED)
descriptions: Implemented in five municipalities in Kosovo and three local self-government units in South Serbia.To ensure that citizens in Kosovo and Serbia are better able to empathise with one another’s perspectives, play active civic roles in society, and celebrate diversity. Grassroots civil society actors are offered capacity-building opportunities as well as funding for local initiatives that aim to improve cooperation between local authorities and residents.

titles: Strengthening Gender Equality and LGBTIQ+ Advocacy Movement
descriptions: The project supports women’s rights and advancing acceptance of LGBTIQ+ individuals in Montenegro. The project aims to transform unequal power relations in society by empowering women and the LGBTIQ+ community and advocating for their rights in Montenegro.

titles: Enabling Merit Based Recruitment in Public Administration (Montenegro)
descriptions: A project to strengthen the merit-based recruitment practices in Montenegro's public administration to enhance the civil service's competence, efficiency, and independence. By addressing the challenges posed by recent amendments to the Law on Civil Servants and State Employees, the project will help create more effective, transparent, and accountable institutions. Through capacity-building, support for refining recruitment procedures, and promoting a culture of fairness, the initiative aims to assist Montenegro’s efforts in streamlining the hiring and retention of skilled civil servants on merit. This, in turn, will foster public trust in institutions and augment Montenegro's overarching political stability and development.

titles: Strengthening Demand for Merit Based Recruitment
descriptions: The project focuses on one of the most pressing fields in Montenegro: public sector recruitment. With the effort of mapping the risks of undue politicisation and corruption during recruitment already conducted, the project will further promote the findings and the recommendations stemming from this pioneering endeavour. It will also ensure new perspectives in this important field, by ensuring continuous monitoring of public sector recruitment procedures, which will result in a number of citizen-facing, public outreach and advocacy activities, which will be largely aligned with the citizens’ concerns, on one hand, and with the Government’s and Parliament’s policy agendas, on the other. The main impact of the project is to increase evidence-based public demand for merit-based recruitment practices across the Montenegrin public sector, and thus, in the long-term contribute to more meritocratic procedures and practices.

titles: Democracy and Resilience in the Western Balkans: Supporting Feminist Change Agents
descriptions: The proposed programme aims to address persistent challenges in the Western Balkans related to growing nationalism and anti-democratic tendencies which are contributing to a shrinking civic space and negative attitudes towards gender equality, women’s rights and LGBT+ community. Responding to these challenges, the overarching goal is to cultivate a vibrant, pluralistic civil society in the Western Balkans that contributes to democracy and the realisation of women's rights and LGBT+ persons’ rights, resulting in a resilient civil society in the Western Balkans. More concretely, the programme takes a two-fold approach to attain this via comprehensive organisational support and capacity development to women’s rights organizations (WROs) and LGBT+ organisations to fortify their work in countering GBV and resisting anti-democratic movements and narratives in the Western Balkans and strengthening inclusive feminist movements.

titles: Srebrenica Memorial Self-Reliance Project - Bosnia and Herzegovina
descriptions: The project seeks to further strengthen SMC’s role as a trusted, professional and referent organization that contributes to remembrance, research, and reconciliation, peace-building and conflict prevention by assisting the self-reliance of SMC in the future and laying the foundations for internal organization growth and enhanced external outreach and recognition. Through institutional development by drafting internal organizational documents, developing practices, ensuring support for internal cohesion and well-being, with a special focus on female members of staff, strategic planning, and outreach through media and exchange programs, the SMC will be equipped with the needed tools to continue its path as a self-sufficient institution of remembrance, education, and research.

titles: Open Data for Open Societies - Serbia
descriptions: This project aims to leverage the benefits of opening, sharing, and collaborating around data to improve the level of democracy, accountability, transparency, and tackle societal challenges. The project will raise the ambition of the public open data ecosystem and elevate use of data as a strategy tool across government, in particular its use in audit and environmental protection. It will improve engagement of public institutions with citizens using open data and build data capabilities in the public sector. The project will empower more women to benefit from data skills and contribute to the use of open data for gender equality.

titles: Leave No One Behind: Fostering Equality and Protection against Discrimination - Serbia
descriptions: The "Leave No One Behind" project aims to promote equality and protect vulnerable groups from discrimination in Serbia. It will introduce systematic changes to policy making processes by developing a methodology that ensures laws and policies consider diversity perspectives. By advocating for a more responsive strategic framework in the area of anti-discrimination and better implementation of planned measures, as well as improving accountability of national and local governments, the project seeks to enhance protection and support mechanisms for citizens facing discrimination. Additionally, by building the capacities of local organisations to provide community-based assistance regarding discrimination, the project will expand direct support to victims nationwide. Through these structural and functional improvements to legislation, strategic frameworks, and support networks, the project strives to create a more equitable and just society where the rights of every individual are protected and no one is left behind.

titles: Empowering Albanian Youth and Enhancing Integration Into Serbian Society - Serbia
descriptions: The project aims to address the challenges faced by the Albanian minority in Serbia, particularly in Presevo and Bujanovac. It focuses on boosting their socio-political integration and representation, while also providing professional development opportunities. Key initiatives include establishing a youth caucus connected to the Serbian Assembly and Serbian national institutions/ministries, facilitating mentorship and networking in various professional fields, offering internships in local institutions, and supporting civil society projects. Additionally, the project promotes intercultural understanding through study visits between Albanian and Serbian youth. The goal of the project is to foster conflict prevention by creation of a more inclusive, harmonious society without ethnic and cultural divides.

titles: Addressing effects of gender based violence in Kosovo and empowering survivors to fight stigma - Kosovo
descriptions: Empowerment of women and girls through tackling conflict related sexual violence, gender based violence and promoting women’s meaningful participation in decision-making processes.

titles: Support civil society to increase public oversight and accountability in Kosovo
descriptions: The project aims to strengthen the Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) watchdog function needed in any democracy to prevent or generate measurable evidence of corruption; help the new government make long awaited changes in the way institutions are run; and tackle corruption and serious organised crime.

titles: Peacebuilding: Supporting Marginalised (ROMA) Communities in BiH
descriptions: The project aims to: a) develop research on the sufferings of the Roma, b) provide a platform to hear the voice of Roma war-time victims and c) design and implement Roma specific commemoration activities.

titles: Reflecting interests of K-Serbs to formulate policy proposals - Kosovo
descriptions: The overall objective of this project is to support the process of integration of the Serb community into the Kosovo constitutional framework by developing tailored policy proposals that address the most critical issues associated with this process. This projects builds on the British Embassy funded project in FY 23/24, 'The Needs of the Kosovo-Serb Community in the Process of normalisation of Relations between Serbia and Kosovo,' published in September 2023, which identified the basic needs of the Serb community in Kosovo and produced a study with a series of recommendations. This project will use those recommendations, focussing on three key issues (security, protection of cultural heritage, and access to documents), and further engagement with citizens, to draft policy proposals that will support the full integration of the Serb community into a stable and democratic Kosovo. The policy proposals will be shared with the Government of Kosovo and international diplomatic corps.

titles: Regional Missing Persons phase 2
descriptions: To safeguard and further advance the result of the past five years of the UK-supported regional cooperation process. The project aims to put in place steps to strengthen and sustain  the Missing Persons Group (MPG),  with active engagement of the families of missing persons.  The overall goal of the project is to ensure continued regional cooperation on the resolution of missing persons issue in the Western Balkans based on the rule of law principles.

titles: Invest in Women: Accelerate Progress towards gender equality in Alban
Invest in Women: Accelerate Progress towards gender equality in Albania
descriptions: The focus of this project is the promotion and protection of human rights of women, with a special focus on i) women journalists and in general women’s rights in the media, as well as the media’s role in promoting gender equality; ii) women professionals, activists and advocates’ rights to access public spaces, especially media, with the aim of enhancing their voices; iii) access of diverse women in vulnerable situations in economic empowerment opportunities, thus promoting their socio-economic rights; iv) women survivors of violence; v) men and boys. Where possible the project will try to employ an intersectional approach to dealing with the issues it tackles especially in highlighting violence against LBT women and the need for economic empowerment of these groups.

titles: Strengthening of Public Procurement in Kosovo
descriptions: This project aims to continue providing support to Procurement Review Board members to ensure high-quality and consistent decision-making and to ensure that the PRB is professionally presented before and accountable to the Assembly Committee. This will improve the sustainability of our project and the value for money.

titles: Bridging Gender Bias in Judiciary - North Macedonia
descriptions: Improved legal system through systematically addressing gender-based stereotypes and biases in the judiciary in North Macedonia, with the development and implementation of evidence-based strategies and policies, and awareness-raising initiatives. This will contribute to promoting gender equality in the court system.

titles: Improving the capacities of journalists in Kosovo on peace journalism
descriptions: This short intervention aims to promote responsible “peace journalism” that contributes to understanding, reconciliation, and sustainable peace in Kosovo through collaborative reporting and exchange with journalists from Northern Ireland.

titles: Secondment to the Office of the High Representative (OHR) - Bosnia and Herzegovina
descriptions: Secondment of a UK official to the Office of the High Representative (OHR) - Bosnia and Herzegovina, to support the delivery of its mandate. This project code covers funding from 1 Sept 2024 - 31 March 2025

titles: Serbian Equality Commission
descriptions: The project seeks to work with and achieve UK buy-in with the (Office of the) Serbian Equality Commissioner and maximise their work on gender equality in Serbia. Via workshops with school children and teachers, the digitalisation of an exhibition about great Serbian women, and the annual conference of the Equality Commissioner, it will spread knowledge about gender equality amongst Serbian youth, highlight discrimination and protection mechanisms, establish curricula and instil this learning for future generations.

titles: Spark - Skilled Youth, Empowered Communities Serbia
descriptions: This project will tackle the deep-rooted issues of division and inter-ethnic tension/mistrust in the southern and southwestern Serbian municipalities of Presevo and Bujanovac, and Novi Pazar. The project will bring together representative constituencies of boys and girls of high school age from the Serb, Bosniak, and Albanian communities in order to break down barriers of separation and build new, positive relationships, alongside trust and understanding.

titles: Montenegro Strengthening legislative processes and inclusive policymaking
descriptions: It will be delivered through facilitating structured cross-party dialogue on the most important legislative pieces that would fall under the ongoing electoral reform, knowledge sharing, and peer-to-peer exchanges that empower women members of parliament (MPs) individually and collectively. These interventions would be complemented by mapping the gaps and structural barriers in parliamentary policies and practices in the areas of the project’s objectives.

titles: Strengthening transitional justice processes in the Western Balkans - Serbia
descriptions: The project aims to enhance accountability for war crimes in the Western Balkans and support regional cooperation among State Prosecutors in bringing perpetrators to justice and processing outstanding cases – as part of the wider efforts in dealing with the legacies of the conflicts from the 1990s. The project will be delivered in synergy with, and complement, ongoing initiatives such as the EU Support to Confidence Building in the Western Balkans, ensuring coherence, avoiding duplication, and maximising collective impact across regional justice and reconciliation efforts.

titles: Secondment to Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) Mission in Kosovo
descriptions: This project will fund the UK’s secondment for the Head of the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) Mission in Kosovo to encourage progress on democracy, stability and security, including a more effective regional approach to tackling the most pertinent threats and to ensuring long-term stability.

titles: Promoting Stability in the Western Balkans - Programme funded in-house delivery roles
descriptions: Having in-house delivery roles will enable Western Balkans’s programming and policy teams, through FRP, to better understand and respond to local political and social dynamics relating to conflict.  This will enable more robust and evidence based programming under FRP and within other programmes in the portfolio, in addition to wider FCDO Western Balkans policy delivery.

titles: Emergency Medical Team response to nightclub fire
descriptions: At around 03:00 local time on Sunday 16 March, a fire broke out in a warehouse nightclub venue in the eastern city of Kocani, around 80km from the capital Skopje, in North Macedonia. FCDO quickly mobilised its Emergency Medical Team (EMT) to support. The intervention is having real impact. The EMT has inserted itself into the heart of the decision making process in the Macedonian and International system, influencing high quality decision making and giving the UK a (disproportionately large) seat around the table

titles: Srebrenica Outreach Project - BiH
descriptions: With the 30th anniversary of the Srebrenica genocide in 2025, the Srebrenica Outreach Project aims to ensure that the benefits gained through previous UK-supported programmes are embedded into the long-term work of the Srebrenica Memorial Centre. After a year of reforming the institution’s internal structure through the Srebrenica Self-Reliance Project, the focus now shifts to strengthening its public engagement and outreach. This next phase will build sustainable initiatives that enhance the Centre’s visibility, reinforce its credibility, and ensure continued support from partners, contributors, and the wider public.

titles: Fighting impunity and promoting transitional justice in Bosnia and Herzegovina
descriptions: The project aims to contribute to a more equitable and reconciled society in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where wartime victims' rights are protected, gender sensitivity in justice and reparations systems is enhanced and where rule of law and transitional justice are respected.

titles: Dayton Peace Agreement (DPA) and Gender - BiH
descriptions: Commissioning a review on the impact of the Dayton Peace Agreement (DPA) for gender equality within Bosnia and Herzegovina. The findings will deepen understanding of the legacy impact this has had on women’s exclusion from institutional processes and functions since the establishment of the DPA, as well as its social consequences. Looking forward, it will highlight the needs and priorities of women, and make an intellectual contribution to the wider evidence base regarding the importance of gender in peace processes and Transitional Justice.

titles: Advancing Roma Participation in Transitional Justice in BiH
descriptions: Providing pathways to justice, recognition and support for Roma war victims in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

titles: Strengthening Albania's resilience against corruption and organised crime through effective communications (SPAK)
descriptions: The project will strengthen the Albanian SPAK (Special Structure against Corruption and Organised Crime) communication capacity to counter misinformation, to build public trust, and support its operational effectiveness in managing communication crisis episodes.

titles: Radio Television of Bosnia and Herzegovina reporting for Berlin Process
descriptions: To enable transparent reporting of the Berlin Process meetings in Bosnia and Herzegovina

titles: Follow the Money: Strengthening Albania’s Anti-Money Laundering Initiatives
descriptions: This project addresses Albania’s systemic gaps in money-laundering prevention and enforcement by combining watchdog journalism, stakeholder engagement, and policy analysis. It will generate independent evidence on high-risk sectors, strengthen the capacity of journalists and gatekeepers, and promote institutional dialogue to close legal and operational loopholes.

titles: Non-Budget Financial Aid to the Government of Jordan/Ministry of Education
descriptions:
Financial Aid to the Government of Jordan for the Accelerating Access Initiative 2.0.

The funding will support the Ministry of Education to provide inclusive, quality education to approximately 155,000 Syrian refugee children and 30,000 non-Syrian refugee children. This includes tuition fees, transportation, teacher-training, learning resources, opening of additional double shift schools, supporting blended and remedial learning and covering costs for operations and equipment in these schools.

Financial Aid to the Government of Jordan for the Accelerating Access Initiative 2.0.The funding will support the Ministry of Education to provide inclusive, quality education to approximately 155,000 Syrian refugee children and 30,000 non-Syrian refugee children. This includes tuition fees, transportation, teacher-training, learning resources, opening of additional double shift schools, supporting blended and remedial learning and covering costs for operations and equipment in these schools.

Through a three-year programme, BRIDGE will champion the UK’s commitment for every girl to receive 12 years of quality education, squarely responding to the FCDO’s priorities on Women and Girls. This programme will provide access to quality education for marginalised children, especially girls, and will support learning recovery for 1.6 million host community and refugee children impacted by almost two years of continuous school closures (due to COVID-19).BRIDGE will ensure inclusion is mainstreamed in Jordan’s education system through: supporting access to education; improving quality of education; building societal and economic resilience; and maximising existing UK contributions.

titles: BRIDGE Rapid/Flexible Technical Assistance Fund
descriptions: The Flexible Technical Assistance Fund will support the Ministry of Education's response to arriving needs and also for the British Embassy Amman Education Team to provide short-term expertise and/or conduct research as and when needed. As a lesson learned from COVID-19, a flexible Technical Assistance approach is needed to rapidly response to emergencies.

titles: Inclusion of vulnerable girls and boys in basic education, including Syrian refugees
descriptions: The project will support UNICEF maintain camp school operations in refugee camps in Jordan.  It will also support assistive devices and transportation for children with disabilities; an out of school children study; and a social and behaviour change study on harm prevention.

titles: Inclusion of vulnerable girls and boys in basic education, including Syrian refugees (UNICEF)
descriptions: The project will support UNICEF maintain camp school operations in refugee camps in Jordan. It will also support assistive devices and transportation for children with disabilities; an out of school children study; and a social and behaviour change study on harm prevention.

titles: Yangambi Engagement Landscape (YEL)
descriptions:
To provide funding and support to the CIFOR-ICRAF’s intervention in the Yangambi Engagement Landscape with the key objectives to: 
- Slow down deforestation and forest degradation through an adoption of non-harmful practices, improving the biodiversity of the landscape.
- To improve human well-being through increased sustainable production and access to alternative sources of income, including employment.
- To improve the local economic fabric through long-term commitment, effective management and direct and indirect benefits of conservation. 
The overall outcome of the project is to preserve biodiversity and improve governance and the standard of living of populations in the Yangambi Landscape through sustainable management of natural resources based on sound practices of conservation, development and support for the local economic fabric.

titles: Congo Rainforest Alliance for Forest Training for Sustainable Development (CRAFT-Sustainable Development)
descriptions: The program will provide underpinning data and understanding needed for policies that slow deforestation, improve livelihoods and support sustainable development. Investing in regionally owned expertise and integrated monitoring will maintain an indispensable flow of new data and advice for decades to come. Key Objectives include: • To understand the value and vulnerability of the Congo Basin. • Build scientific capacity and capability in Central Africa. • Translate science for policy and community action.

titles: CBFA Programme Funded Advisers
descriptions: Funding for CBFA Programme Funded Advisers to ensure effective programme delivery, programme stakeholder engagement as well as providing support to Post.

titles: Conferences & Events
Policy and Partnership engagement in the Congo Basin
descriptions: Funding for Conferences and Events related to the CBFA programme, initially to agree on a process to deliver a second Congo Basin Pledge at COP30.
Funding towards building Partnerships and to contribute toward Policy engagements within the Congo Basin.

titles: Emergency health assistance to India
descriptions: Provision of medical equipment to support the Government of India’s response to COVID-19. The programme will provide oxygen concentrators, ventilators and oxygen generators which will enable vital medical treatment to those suffering from COVID-19 in India.

titles: SIMAP - Global Evaluation & Monitoring Framework Agreement contract
descriptions: Contract for delivery of the Sudan Independent Monitoring & Analysis Programme (SIMAP) procured through the FCDO's Global Evaluation & Monitoring Framework (GEMFA). SIMAP will support BE Khartoum's bilateral policy and programme portfolio to improve effectiveness through providing timely and objective information on delivery and contextual developments. The programme will work with a commercial supplier to deploy thematic and contextual experts throughout Sudan to conduct in-person and/or remote monitoring and capacity building activities. The three main workstreams, which align with the outcomes articulated in the programme Theory of Change, are: (i) Assurance & Capacity Building: Field-based monitoring of programme delivery and results; assessments of implementing partner systems for collecting programme information and meeting FCDO priority compliance requirements, including making recommendations for improvements and providing targeted technical assistance. (ii) Learning & Innovation: Design and implementation of a learning strategy to support FCDO and its partners with synthesising and acting on data and evidence generated by the programme and FCDO’s wider portfolio in Sudan; delivery of action learning research projects to test the potential of new and/or innovative approaches to policy or programme delivery, and enhanced collection of beneficiary feedback to inform the design and/or implementation of FCDO policy and programmes; (iii) Strategy & Analysis: Demand-led research and analytical pieces on topics of strategic interest to the FCDO in Sudan, including desk-based reviews drawing on secondary sources and primary research conducted in Sudan.

titles: Programme-Funded Staff and In-House Delivery
descriptions: This project code will only be used for a programme-funded role, where in house delivery options has been proven to be a better alternative on value for money bases.

titles: Nutrition Draught Response through WFP
Prevention and treatment of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (World Food Programme)
World Food Programme (WFP)-RDEL
descriptions: Prevention and treatment of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) amongst children and pregnant and breast-feeding women.

The Ethiopia Crises to Resilience (EC2R) programme is aimed to alleviate the impact of the conflict and drought on the poorest Ethiopians. The programme tries to address urgent humanitarian needs while maintaining the delivery of essential services across the country.

titles: Emergency Health Response in Conflict affected areas - WHO
descriptions: The Ethiopia Crises to Resilience (EC2R) programme is aimed to alleviate the impact of the conflict and drought on the poorest Ethiopians. The programme tries to address urgent humanitarian needs while maintaining the delivery of essential services across the country.

titles: Ethiopia adaptive safety net project - Cash and food transfer to chronically food insecure households
Productive Safety Net Programme (World Bank)
World Bank (WB)-RDEL
descriptions: Cash and food transfers to chronically food insecure households through Ethiopia's rural social protection system.

The Ethiopia Crises to Resilience (EC2R) programme is aimed to alleviate the impact of the conflict and drought on the poorest Ethiopians. The programme tries to address urgent humanitarian needs while maintaining the delivery of essential services across the country.

titles: Ethiopia's adaptive safety net project - Public works (ICF)

titles: Supporting enabling conditions for sustainable agricultural commodities in Bolivia
descriptions:
The project will strengthen existing governance mechanisms (roundtables) to enable Bolivia to shift towards more sustainable DCF soy and beef production. First, we will organise one event with international actors (e.g. 3 Keel/Soy Retail Group, microfinance companies) to highlight DCF commitments and initiatives in the region as well as how this can benefit the Bolivian soy sector. This event will aim to make DCF a central issue for the soy governance roundtable and will be organised with CAO (Agricultural chamber of Bolivia) and other soy sector organisations. 
    
Second, we will facilitate a peer-to-peer learning exchange on sustainable beef value chains. This will draw on 10+ years of UK support for this sector in Colombia, including the current UK PACT/WWF project with Grupo Exito.  Through the exchange, cattle ranchers of the Federation of Cattle Ranchers of Santa Cruz , other beef producers, and retailers will learn about standards and practices involved in development of a sustainable beef value chain. Our expectation is that beef sector actors in Bolivia will then explore how to adapt this learning to their context.    As deforestation is the largest source of emissions, these actions will contribute to Bolivia´s efforts to deliver on its new NDC commitments, and the implementation of UK’s Amazon Pledge.
